heading: 8.4 Dimensioned × dimensioned — strip and assert
text:
### 8.4 Dimensioned × dimensioned — strip and assert [LUNI.8.4]

No unit algebra. `*` of two dimensioned values, `/` and `//` of two values of
different dimensions, `/` and `//` of a bare number by a dimensioned value, and `**` with a dimensioned operand on either side
produce a result with no dimension DS can state. The compiler **must** refuse each
with `DS_VALIDATE_DIM_AMBIGUOUS`, under a `let` annotation too: an annotation
checks a type the value already has ([LUNI.8.6]). An author who wants the raw
numeric result strips the units on the operands first, and may assert a unit on
the result: `(r.w::Float * r.h::Float)::meter_squared`.

The strip yields base-unit numbers and the assertion applies no factor
([LUNI.8.5]), so the scale of the result is the author's to state. A value of the
`time` dimension strips to nanoseconds ([LUNI.7.2]).

This rule applies to both scalar and complex dimensioned values. The built-in
library pre-declares common multiplication results (e.g. `watt` = `volt × ampere`,
`joule` = `newton × meter`), so those results have a unit to assert.

alloy.name: luni_8_4__product_needs_annotation
alloy.note: The model's one `Mult` class accepts any two dimensioned operands under an annotation and refuses them without one. The clause admits a same-dimension `/` and `//` with no annotation, and refuses the rest with or without one.
